General_Description.Text: CUBIC (clear, unobstructed brain/body imaging cocktails and computational analysis) is a hydrophilic tissue clearing method that enables whole organ and body imaging with single-cell resolution. It involves the strategic integration of optimal chemical cocktails for tissue delipidation, decoloring, refractive index matching, and decalcification. The updated CUBIC protocols are scalable and reproducible, allowing for the efficient clearing of mouse organs, mouse body including bone, and large primate and human tissues. CUBIC-treated tissues are transparent enough to detect almost all cells at the whole-organ scale, and the protocol is compatible with fluorescent protein visualization.

Tissue_Types.Text: CUBIC protocol II can efficiently clear the whole body of a P7 mouse.
Text_Reference: Results Section: 'Scalable Imaging of Mouse Whole Body, Including the Inside of Bone, and Large Human Organ Blocks by CUBIC Protocols.':To perform exhaustive whole-body imaging, we applied CUBIC protocol II to render transparent the whole body of a P7 mouse and stained it with nuclear-staining dye (Figure 6A; Video S1).

Tissue_Types.Text: CUBIC protocol III was applied to large human tissue blocks, including lung, kidneys, and liver.
Text_Reference: Results Section,'Scalable Imaging of Mouse Whole Body, Including the Inside of Bone, and Large Human Organ Blocks by CUBIC Protocols':'To examine the scalability of the CUBIC protocols, we applied CUBIC protocol III to large human tissue blocks; a large chunk of dissected human lung (approximately 43.4 x 16.0 x 26.4 mm3; Figure S6L; Video S2), dissected human kidneys (Figure S6N), and a dissected human liver.'

Tissue_Types.Text: CUBIC protocol I was applied to the brain of a 1-year-old male marmoset.
Text_Reference: Results Section,'Scalable Imaging of Mouse Whole Body, Including the Inside of Bone, and Large Human Organ Blocks by CUBIC Protocols':'We next performed the whole-brain imaging of an adult marmoset. The brain of a 1-year-old male marmoset was cleared using a modified CUBIC protocol I with propidium iodide (PI) staining, resulting in a cleared PI-stained brain without apparent morphological distortion (Figure S6R).'

Time_Consumption.Text1: CUBIC protocol I for adult mouse organ samples requires 3-7 days for delipidation at 37°C.
Text1_Reference: CUBIC Protocols section: 'The organs in CUBIC-L were incubated with shaking at 37°C for 3-7 days.'

Time_Consumption.Text2: CUBIC protocol II for mouse body or tissues that include bone requires 3-7 days for delipidation at 37°C, followed by 5-7 days for decalciﬁcation at 37°C.
Text2_Reference: CUBIC Protocols section: 'PFA-fixed samples were immersed in CUBIC-L with shaking at 37°C for 3-7 days, then washed with PBS at room temperature overnight.'
CUBIC Protocols section: 'The samples were immersed in CUBIC-B with shaking at 37°C for 5-7 days, then washed with PBS at room temperature overnight.'

Time_Consumption.Text3: CUBIC protocol III for aggressive tissue clearing requires 1-2 weeks for delipidation at 37°C or 45°C.
Text3_Reference: CUBIC Protocols section: 'The tissue blocks were immersed in CUBIC-HL with shaking at 37°C (for human brain or kidney) or 45°C (for human heart, liver, lung, or spleen) for 1-2 weeks.'

Time_Consumption.Text4: CUBIC protocol IV for large blocks of human brain tissue requires 1-2 weeks for delipidation at 45°C.
Text4_Reference: CUBIC Protocols section: 'The brain blocks were immersed in CUBIC-L with shaking at 45°C for 1-2 weeks, then washed with PBS at room temperature.'

Application.Text4: CUBIC protocol II enables brain and spine imaging at single-cell resolution in the skull and backbone, even in adult mice.
Text4_Reference: Results Section, 'Scalable Imaging of Mouse Whole Body, Including the Inside of Bone, and Large Human Organ Blocks by CUBIC Protocols': 'CUBIC protocol II enabled brain and spine imaging at single-cell resolution in the skull and backbone.'

Application.Text5: CUBIC protocol III enables volumetric imaging of human kidney at single-cell resolution, allowing identification and segmentation of glomeruli.
Text5_Reference: Results Section, 'Scalable Imaging of Mouse Whole Body, Including the Inside of Bone, and Large Human Organ Blocks by CUBIC Protocols': 'To examine the feasibility of volumetric imaging of human kidney at single-cell resolution, we visualized the 3D structure of the glomerulus after nuclear staining.'

Application.Text6: CUBIC protocols facilitate comprehensive cell analysis at the whole-organ scale, such as segmentation of the glomeruli in a mouse kidney and whole-organ cell detection in the liver and lung of a mouse.
Text6_Reference: Results Section, 'Inspection of the Tissue Integrity of CUBIC-Treated Organs': 'We also applied our CUBIC protocols to comprehensive cell analysis at the whole-organ scale... The application of the CUBIC protocol I revealed comprehensive segmentation of the glomeruli in a mouse kidney and whole-organ cell detection in the left medial lobe of the liver and left lung of a mouse.'

Application.Text7: CUBIC protocol II was applied to a mouse model to observe the infiltration of metastatic cancer cells from bone to adjacent soft tissues in the leg, and to visualize metastatic bone tumors through the skull.
Text7_Reference: Results Section: 'next, we applied this protocol to metastatic bone tumors in the leg of an MDA-231-D-injected mouse (Figures 6E–6H and S6I) and observed the infiltration of metastatic cancer cells from bone tissue to the adjacent soft tissues. The metastatic bone tumors were even visible through skull (Figures S6J and S6K)'

Application.Text: CUBIC protocol I enables virtual multiplex whole-brain imaging without significant quenching of fluorescent proteins (FPs), allowing for the comparative analysis of various genetically labeled cell types, including different neurons, glial cells, and metastatic cancer cells.
Text_Reference: Results Section: 'Simple immersion-based CUBIC protocols should be applicable and highly reproducible for tissue clearing without the significant quenching of FPs. We next used CUBIC protocol I combined with the visualization of a series of fluorescently labeled mouse samples.'

'...All of the brains were treated with a nuclear staining dye (RedDot2) for registration... We registered the nuclear images to that of a reference brain, and directly compared the FP signals by overlaying their registered images... thus achieving virtual multiplex whole-brain imaging.'

'The overlaid image made it possible to compare the global distribution of pyramidal neurons (Thy1-YFP), astrocytes (Mlc1-YFP), oligodendrocytes (Plp-YFP), dopaminergic neurons (Th-EGFP), serotonin receptor 5B (Htr5b-YFP), and dopamine receptor D1 (Drd1-mVenus) at the whole-brain scale.'

'Furthermore, FP expressed in metastatic tumor cells (MDA-231-D cancer cells expressing mCherry) was also clearly visible using our CUBIC protocol I, allowing the morphological analysis of cancer metastasis.'

Note.Text1: The refractive index matching reagent achieves a high refractive index while maintaining water-like viscosity.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section, 'RI Matching': 'To develop an alternative high-RI medium based on hydrophilic chemicals...'

Note.Text2: The delipidation efficiency, especially for the phospholipid content, was correlated with the final tissue transparency, indicating that delipidation is essential for thorough tissue clearing.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Delipidation and Decoloring': 'Next, we measured the residual phospholipid and cholesterol contents of mouse brains treated with the chemicals and evaluated the relative transmittance of these brains after RI matching...'

Note.Text3: N-alkylimidazole showed a low delipidation efficiency.
Text3_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Delipidation and Decoloring': 'However, since N-alkylimidazole showed a low delipidation efficiency...'

Note.Text5: The updated CUBIC protocols have a few potential limitations, including the degradation of almost all endogenous RNA and the disappearance of much of the presynaptic and postsynaptic fabric with thorough delipidation.
Text5_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'Our updated protocols have a few potential limitations. Since both of the delipidation cocktails are alkaline-buffered solutions, almost all of the endogenous RNA would be degraded...'

Text7_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Inspection of the Tissue Integrity of CUBIC-Treated Organs': 'Because the final morphology of tissues was influenced by the pH of CUBIC-R...'

Note.Text8: The proposed protocols largely retain the amount and antigenicity of the proteins.
Text8_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Inspection of the Tissue Integrity of CUBIC-Treated Organs': 'These findings indicated that the proposed protocols largely retain the amount and antigenicity of the proteins.'
